image_prompt.text: A chain of coral heads, rock shelves and sunken platforms spaced to jump limits, forming the ordered route across the seabed
Flat enclosed pads on the seabed route where players stop safely between sections
Long horizontal gaps between reef outcrops, bounce pads and stepped coral ledges
Drifting and rotating platforms, current-driven conveyors and swinging kelp hazards

layout_placement.text: Respawn points at each safe pad so failure returns the player to the last section rather than the start

notes: Shape was not stated; a flat seabed course was assumed via the Classic Obby preset.
The setting is submerged. P6 spacing is derived from default WalkSpeed/JumpHeight on dry ground, so confirm whether the player swims or walks before generating.

answers.ask: Should the course run flat along the ocean floor, or climb toward the surface as a tower?
answers.answer: Make it a compact course that climbs from the ocean floor toward the surface.

answers.ask: Is this one continuous course or a series of numbered stages, and how hard should it be?
answers.answer: Use one continuous, easy-to-medium difficulty course with checkpoints along the way.

answers.answer: The player should walk and jump on a dry seabed, with the ocean surrounding it as the backdrop.
